text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.67% today to $154.03, the highest close in the past two weeks, as oil prices surged and geopolitical tensions eased slightly. U.S. crude rose above $103 a barrel while global crude hit $123—both strong levels—partly on news that Qatari mediators held extensive talks in Tehran aimed at restarting U.S.-Iran negotiations, reducing the immediate risk of further escalation in the Middle East. That reduction in geopolitical risk, combined with firm oil prices, lifted the stock after it had dipped below $148 just two days earlier.

The broader picture reinforces the move: refining earnings across Big Oil have surged as fuel supplies tightened, and even though gasoline prices have risen despite Trump's campaign promises to cut them, tankers continue moving crude through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iranian attacks, keeping supply flowing at higher freight rates. For an integrated oil company like ConocoPhillips, stronger crude prices and tighter refining margins both work in the same direction.
